topics.title: 课程作业
topics.summary: ETH Zurich advocates a proactive and responsible approach to generative AI in coursework. Students remain fully responsible for the content of any work they submit. Generative AI may serve a supplementary role (such as brainstorming, structuring, or coding assistance), but must never replace personal effort. Lecturers hold authority to determine whether and how generative AI may be used in their courses.

topics.title: 使用披露
topics.summary: ETH Zurich's declaration of originality provides two options: confirming that no generative AI was used, or confirming that authorised generative AI was used and its disclosure agreed with the supervisor. Bachelor's and Master's theses require a signed declaration of originality, while requirements for other written assessments depend on the applicable academic instructions. Doctoral candidates declare independent authorship through the doctoral examination registration process. The permitted use, disclosure format and any exceptions must follow the relevant supervisor and unit requirements. ETH Zurich's teaching guidelines instruct students to be transparent about their use of generative AI and to identify which tools contributed to which parts of their work, in accordance with applicable lecturer instructions and citation conventions. For scientific writing and theses, students should agree in advance with their supervisors on authorised AI use and disclosure requirements. ETH Library guidance recognises an exception where a supervisor has expressly agreed that particular AI use need not be separately declared. In the absence of such an agreement, undeclared use may constitute a breach of academic integrity.
topics.scope: Follow the cited course, supervisor, degree, research or service-specific conditions; local reviewed candidate, not a published student snapshot.

topics.title: 隐私与敏感数据
topics.summary: Uploading strictly confidential information to external cloud AI services is prohibited. Confidential information may only be processed in specifically evaluated configurations (such as M365 Copilot Work mode without web search). M365 Copilot Chat is approved for internal data. Google AI tools have not yet been assessed by the CISO (assessment OPEN) and are not released for ETH confidential, strictly confidential, or protected personal data. Copyright and privacy must be respected at all times.

topics.title: 研究与发表
topics.summary: Researchers and students are fully responsible for the integrity of their scientific work and must verify AI-generated output, references, and facts. Generative AI tools cannot be listed as authors or cited as authoritative sources. Theses require signed originality declarations; doctoral candidates declare independent authorship upon registration for the doctoral examination. Researchers must comply with applicable funder (e.g. SNSF) and publisher guidelines.

additionalTopics.title: 学术诚信
additionalTopics.summary: ETH Library provides Turnitin Originality to eligible professors and lecturers for text-similarity checking, subject to data classification and responsible selective-use guidance. Only public or internal documents may be uploaded. Similarity screening is distinct from AI-authorship detection; ETH Zurich warns that technical detection of AI-generated output is unreliable and should not be treated as conclusive evidence. Violations of GenAI guidelines such as use of unauthorised aids or non-disclosure of their use are subject to disciplinary action under existing performance assessment rules and the declaration of originality.
